Reproduced pool ranks: EsDeeKid's own 3.72M-play master at 29/460 behind 28 edit-titled rows; 'Rae Sremmurd - No Type (Official Video)' at 938M plays at rank 52/558 with ranks 1-51 all 51/51 edit-titled; Mac Miller's plain rows at 38-41 of 433 with 259/433 edit-titled; 'Katy Perry - Roar' at 4.37 BILLION plays at rank 75/518. The structural half, which makes this a defect rather than a tuning miss: `is_official_original` (4852) requires `not EDIT_WORDS.search(c["title"])`, which is the SAME predicate `edit_titled` negates, so the rows rank_key's plain-original tier at 5216 is built to prefer on an unedited clip are exactly the rows the download queue guarantees will not exist - that tier has probably never fired on a popular track, because a viral song always has more than 14 edit-titled uploads. `_dl_priority` also has no uploader-identity leg at all: its `-_artist_hit` leg is a substring test over title+uploader that passed 43 of 164 relevant rows on clip 3 while only 2 rows had the artist as the actual uploader. Three windows requires dur >= 14.0s exactly. Below that, `confirm_ref` returns False for every possible reference regardless of match quality, so both arms of the reference block at server.py:1689-1729 come back empty, `measure_consensus` is never called, `measured` stays None, and `res["speed"]` keeps the phase-1 Shazam counter-sweep placeholder. On clip 26 the engine had already downloaded four clean masters and one produced two windows agreeing to 0.1% at conf 0.56 and 0.48 - refused on COUNT, not quality; bypassing the gate on those same files returns `{speed: 0.9327, label: 'slowed ~0.93x', confident: true, agree: 4/4, spread: 0.002}`, which is the owner's verdict from the engine's own code. Zero exceptions, perfect separation at exactly the constant. A controlled truncation ladder on a synthetic same-recording pair puts the cliff at 14.0s to the tenth of a second.
root_causes.fix: One function, speed_from_master.py:119. Derive the stride from the clip instead of hardcoding it: compute dur first and, when floor((dur-6)/step)+1 < min_win, drop to W=8.0/step=2.0 (and W=6.5/step=1.5 under ~9s). Bit-for-bit no-op for every clip >= 14s, so no long clip's behaviour moves. Measured on clip 30: the right reference goes from 2 windows to 3 tight ones at 0.5751/0.5754/0.5760, confirm_ref returns True with min_win untouched, and the label ships. root_causes.mechanism: An inverted edit_label steered every query in the wrong tempo direction and pushed the one corrective query past a hard cap, so the answer was never in the pool. Three measured links. First, `_consensus_id` (crate_engine.py:2044-2090) ends `return min(pool, key=lambda h: len(h.get("title") or ""))`; inside the winning group every title is the same string so the length key is a no-op and Python's `min` returns the FIRST-INSERTED hit, and insertion order is FINE_SWEEP order (1815-1821), which front-loads all five sped-up counter-rates ahead of every slowed one. Any clip that answers at both a low and a high counter-rate is therefore DETERMINISTICALLY labelled sped up - reversing the input list flips the reported direction in pure Python. This clip measures 0.9002x slowed against the official master (core 1.000 at five offsets, speed 0.9002 at all 21 windows) and shipped 'sped up ~1.11x', the reciprocal. Second, `build_queries` sets `edit_word` from `edit_label` at 3281, so five of the sixteen surviving slots go to sped-up variants, and the UNCONDITIONAL slowed / slowed-reverb safety net at 3364-3371 - added after the Trophies clip for exactly this failure - lands at positions 18 and 19 and is cut by `return q[:16]` at 3375. With the correct label, 'Fetty Wap Trap Queen slowed' sits at position 10, inside the cap. Third, the 16 emitted queries returned 289 rows containing ZERO of the five correct slowed uploads, while query #18 alone returns all five in 1.9s. The engine's own correct reading exists (speed_measured 0.9015, speed_confirmed true) but is produced by `measure_consensus` at server.py:1724, 118 lines AFTER `E.find_edit(... edit_label ...)` at 1606, so it can never reach the search.
root_causes.fix: Most surgical single edit: crate_engine.py:3375, `return q[:16]` -> `return q[:19]`. Purely additive - positions 1 through 16 were verified identical under both the wrong and the right label, so no existing query moves and no other clip's pool reorders. Costs three more concurrent SoundCloud plus YouTube round trips, measured at 1.2-1.9s each fired concurrently. Two ranking-path follow-ups, neither needed for this clip and both requiring the full gate: repair `_consensus_id`'s tie-break so it breaks on which counter-rate actually restored the audio instead of on FINE_SWEEP insertion order; and after `measure_consensus`, when speed_confirmed is true and speed_measured contradicts the DIRECTION of the edit_label that built the queries, overwrite edit_label too and not just `speed`, since today the payload ships 0.9015 and 'sped up ~1.11x' side by side.

Medium for the `_consensus_id` tie-break, which is a ranking-path change on every pitched clip. Honest limit: the cap raise delivers NOTHING on this clip by itself. root_causes.mechanism: The base song ID is wrong and the engine ships it as fact because the one gate designed to catch exactly this has its audio input hardcoded to None. `wrong_song.shazam_untrustworthy(base_title, base_artist, freqskew, corpus_titles, master_core)` computes `master_fail = master_core is not None and master_core < 0.35` (wrong_song.py:46) and `untrust = bool(strong) or master_fail or (len(reasons) >= 2)` (line 50), and its own docstring at lines 7-8 tells the caller to compute master_core as verify(clip, master_of(base))['core']. There is exactly ONE call site in the tree and it passes the literal `None` - I confirmed this directly at server.py:863-864. On this clip the named artist's own master reads core 0.024 against the clip on its first 20s and the exact Shazam track reads 0.308, both under the module's own threshold, while the real song (Gwen Stefani 'Hollaback Girl' instrumental at 0.900x) reads 0.977 with a time-reversed null of 0.201. Running the real function: with None it returns (False, ['base-title-absent-from-...']) - one reason, one short of the len>=2 trip - and with 0.024, 0.147 or 0.340 it returns True at every value. One argument is the entire difference between a 'found' verdict with an exact=true Apple Music link and the honest 'uncertain' that server.py:1936-1953 already knows how to emit. Nothing downstream can recover: `base_uncertain` (1936) is reachable ONLY from `res["shazam_suspect"]`, which only that crippled call sets, and `result = "found"` at 1949 fires on the mere existence of a Shazam fp. Two independent audio measurements were screaming 'not this song' - 14 downloaded candidates all failing CORE_KEEP with a top core of 0.147, and an empty confirm_ref set - and neither has a wire to the decision. The masters needed are already downloaded: server.py:1697-1712 fetches the base song's official originals in the same request.
root_causes.fix: Inside the master-fetch block at server.py:1697-1725, after `got` is built, compute `master_core = max((V.verify(src["audio"], p) or {}).get("core") or 0.0 for p in got)` and re-run `wrong_song.shazam_untrustworthy` with it; if it now returns untrust, set `res["shazam_suspect"] = why`. The block at 1936 then flips base_uncertain, blanks base_song/base_artist, and 1949 emits `result: "uncertain"` - machinery that is already written and tested. Cost is one V.verify per already-downloaded file, no extra network and no extra Shazam probe. It must live inside that block rather than at line 863, because 863 runs in phase 1 before any audio exists (which is why the None is there) and the fetch at 1689 is itself gated on `shazam_reliable`.
root_causes.risk: Low to medium. It downgrades BASE-ID confidence only and must never touch candidate ranking; the 0.35 threshold sits under CORE_MERIT 0.38 and CORE_KEEP 0.50 so it cannot fire while a real match is in the pool, which keeps it inside the 'bass and speed nudge, never reject' doctrine. The real exposure is that it can turn a currently-'found' answer into 'uncertain' on any clip where the master fetch scores low for an innocent reason, so the gate check is that none of the five regression clips flips to uncertain. Honest limit on the outcome: the best reachable result here is 'uncertain', not the right song - the credit is a bare 'Original audio - togi', desc is empty and there are no comment hints, so with the base name discredited the engine has nothing left to query.

root_causes.mechanism: The engine never learned the SECOND song's name, and without that name the candidate pool is unrankable. The clip is a SEQUENTIAL mashup with the first song occupying only ~2.5-3s, and `_scan_windows(19.069)` returns exactly [0.0, 6.0, 12.0] at span=12 (crate_engine.py:1830), so the lead-in occupies at most 3 of the 12 seconds of window 0 and 0 seconds of windows 1 and 2. Shazam therefore names the second song in all three, `annotate_mashup` hits its tier-1 unanimity gate `if len(order) < 2:` (2589) and returns before tier 2 ever runs. MASHUP_SPAN = 4 (2490) is precisely the resolution a 3s section needs, and it is locked behind a tier-1 disagreement that a section shorter than half a scan window can never produce. Measured at 4s resolution the split is unambiguous - clip[0-4] matches song A at fp 0.906 / arr 0.748 and song B at only arr 0.268, and by clip[3-7] that reverses completely - which is also why two of the three per-clip analyses mistakenly called it 'layered': at whole-clip or 20s resolution a 3s section drowns. With `pair` left None the hint/pair FAST PATH at 4177-4243 never arms, and that lane is the only one that could have won: it runs its own `search_edits(hq, 6)[:FAST_POOL]` with FAST_POOL = 6, bypasses `_dl_priority` entirely, and the pair queries were measured to put the correct upload at search position 1 of 130. Instead the engine fell through to the generic pool where the right row WAS returned but sat at rank 187 of 282 against max_dl = 14, because with key_terms = {'pole'} it and 86 other mashup-shaped rows are literally indistinguishable to `_dl_priority`.
root_causes.fix: Add a probe-free dissent test after the crown is picked, and let ONLY that dissent unlock the tier-2 probes. Cut the clip into MASHUP_SPAN (4s) windows and V.verify each against the crowned candidate's audio, which is already downloaded and on disk; flag a window whose arr falls to roughly a third of the median of the others. On this clip that is unambiguous and costs zero Shazam probes: clip[0-4] arr 0.189 against 0.534-0.712 for every other window. Only on that flag, spend the existing MASHUP_BUDGET tier-2 probes on the flagged region, which is exactly what MASHUP_SPAN = 4 was built to resolve. Do not touch the tier-1 gate and do not reintroduce the blind hidden-layer branch. Do NOT ship the three download-side fixes proposed elsewhere - all three were tested against the saved 282-row pool and all three fail (exempting mashup-shaped rows from the artist-hit rung reaches rank 160, seeding genre_hit reaches rank 180, and a reserved mashup quota selects two wrong uploads); they fail for one shared reason, that 87 rows carry the same key term and nothing in `_dl_priority` can tell them apart until the second song has a name.
root_causes.risk: Low to medium. On a single-song clip every window matches the crown, nothing fires, no probe is spent, and the five regression crowns cannot move. It does spend Shazam probes when it fires, which touches the throttle rule - but only after a MEASURED dissent rather than speculatively, which is the correct posture and is cheaper than the current speculative sweeps. The residual is that a genuinely layered clip (as opposed to sequential) may not produce an arr dip, so this catches sequential mashups and not layered ones; that is a coverage limit, not a regression.

root_causes.mechanism: The literal word `instrumental` inside OTHER_RENDITION (crate_engine.py:3947, which I read directly and confirmed contains cover|guitar|piano|live|instrumental|acoustic|karaoke|remaster|1 hour|hour loop) demotes the correct upload TWICE on title alone, and nothing anywhere in the pipeline ever asks whether the CLIP has vocals. Stage 1, download selection: `_dl_priority` computes `edit_titled = bool(EDIT_WORDS.search(t)) and not OTHER_RENDITION.search(t)` at 4453, so every instrumental is forced to edit_titled=False and sorts below every row whose title says bass/slowed/remix/album version - 'Lil Wayne Lollipop Instrumental' at 3.16M plays lands at rank 104 of 442 against max_dl = 14, and deleting ONLY the `and not OTHER_RENDITION.search(t)` clause moves that exact row to rank 10. Stage 2, ranking: the same regex sets `not_other = False` (4784) and `_rendition_loses` (5026-5027) returns True whenever a non-rendition rival sits within 0.05 core, which is automatic once both saturate, and it is rank_key tier 4, ABOVE speed, bass, core and plays - so even after the download fix the 18.3M-play 'Lollipop (Album Version (Explicit))', already in wave1 slot 7, crowns the instrumental out. Stage 3, independently fatal: `dl_clip` sections *0-20 and on its first 20s the true instrumental reads core 0.4433, under CORE_KEEP 0.50, versus 1.000 at 13 of 23 sliding windows. The clip genuinely IS the instrumental - whisper transcribes the clip and the instrumental as '(upbeat music)' with no words anywhere, while the vocal master returns Lollipop lyrics at exactly the offsets (t=20, 30) that match the clip at core 1.000. Every single-leg counterfactual was run and every one leaves the answer wrong: download-only takes the visible score from 0.241 to 0.443 and stays unsure; window-only crowns the vocal Album Version, which is precisely the complaint; download plus window still hands the crown to the vocal via `_rendition_loses`.
root_causes.fix: Three coupled changes, all required. (1) crate_engine.py:3947, split OTHER_RENDITION into PERFORMANCE_RENDITION (cover|guitar|piano|live|acoustic|karaoke|remaster|1 hour|hour loop) and STEM_RENDITION (instrumental), and have `edit_titled` at 4453 exclude only PERFORMANCE_RENDITION - an instrumental is the same master with a stem muted, a guitar cover is a different performance. Measured effect of exactly that clause: rank 104 -> rank 10, inside the 14 slots, and it changes only what gets a download slot. (2) Ship it with the decode-window work or the download fix is inert. (3) Make `_rendition_loses` (5026) SIGNED and gate it on vocal presence measured ONCE on the CLIP and cached on clip_ctx beside tilt and slope - demote a stem rendition when the clip has speech, PREFER it when it does not. Do NOT use an arr-margin tiebreak: across the windows where each candidate reaches its top score the instrumental's arr spans 0.5002-0.7566 and the vocal's 0.3854-0.5110, so the worst-case margin is -0.0108, and a 0.15 bar would silently fail here.
root_causes.risk: High. Three changes, one of which is the largest ticket on the board, and `_rendition_loses` is a rank_key tier that fires on every clip with a rendition-titled row. The regression case that must not break is the Zelgin Jackson '(Official Instrumental)' miss the rule was written for (documented in the comment at 5015-5019) - a signed rule fixes that one in the correct direction rather than trading it away - and the Anytunz '(Marimba Ringtone Cover)' case, which is a PERFORMANCE rendition and is untouched by the split. Five-clip gate twice. Separate low-priority ticket, not required here: build_queries emits no instrumental lane at all and 9 of its 16 hard-capped slots went to caption noise on this clip; the instrumental was still reachable without it, so that is depth, not the cause.
